artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: Portal worktree commit b67fdb22 on branch wk-DSGN_IRPTV1-34-portal (LOCAL). Row W29-S9's 1-of-3 flake is real filesystem state: this box's core.autocrlf=true (no .gitattributes) checks out the committed contracts/wire/*.ts as CRLF while gen-wire.ts's writeFileSync always emits LF -- the FIRST run against a fresh checkout drifts on EOL alone, then generate()'s own write leaves the tree LF-normalized so later runs agree. Fixed by folding CRLF to LF on both the before and after snapshots before comparing (normalizeEol()), which does not hide a real content drift (still differs after normalization).

Portal worktree commit b67fdb22. Pins the child `bun test` invocation to a fixed numeric --seed=20260927 (never --randomize, so bun's own default, verified-stable file-discovery order holds; --concurrent never passed). collectFailures()'s regex fixed: the original's greedy [^>]*  attrs capture swallowed a self-closed testcase's trailing '/', so its optional tail group scanned past every following passing testcase to the NEXT real </testcase>, misattributing that failure to an earlier, unrelated, passing testcase (verified reproduced on a hand-built 4-testcase pass/pass/fail/pass sample: original misattributes to testcase 1 and loses 2-3; fixed version attributes correctly to testcase 3 and visits all four).

Portal worktree commit b67fdb22. Same --seed pin and collectFailures() fix as s7-determinism-check.ts; the bar is corrected from exact-match to SUBSET per this task order's own stated pass condition (a Q row not currently failing no longer fails the check; a failure outside Q still does -- missingFromQ.length===0 alone decides `ok`, qNotFailing is informational only).

Portal worktree commit 851f3830 on branch wk-DSGN_IRPTV1-34-portal (LOCAL). Adds the row-W29-S9 entry for iv-e-26.wire-regen.test.ts naming the real CRLF/LF source and removing_commit b67fdb22; corrects the top-level note that the earlier 'two internally-stable regimes' read (W29-S10) was very likely an artifact of the collectFailures() misattribution bug, not corpus-wide scheduler variance.
